text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Friday:
- TAG Heuer, a manufacturer of luxury sport watches, reported a 1.2 percent first-quarter net sales increase to 109.7 million Swiss francs compared with the same period in 1996.
- Canon (Schweiz) registered a group profit of 16.5 million Swiss francs for 1996, up from 11.3 million in 1995, despite a 17.1 percent sales decline.

- Swiss Bank Corporation said on Thursday it agreed to buy Wall Street investment bank Dillon Read & Co. for $600 million. The deal still has to be approved by the U.S. Federal Reserve. Founded in 1832, Dillon Read is the oldest investment bank in the U.S.
- U.S. President Clinton said on Thursday that Switzerland deserves applause for its recent efforts to aid Holocaust victims.
- Sales of new automobiles in Switzerland rose by 12 percent in April to 32,784. Sales fell by 2.9 percent to 95,712 from January to April.

- Swiss Task Force Leader Thomas Borer complained to U.S. Senator Alfonse D'Amato about continuous criticism of Switzerland, despite the country's recent efforts regarding funds of Holocaust victims and Nazi gold.
